title: Exogenous treatment of Arabidopsis seedlings with lyso-phospholipids for the inducible complementation of lipid mutants
protocol: Prepare 12-well plates containing 2 mL of ½ MS liquid media supplemented or not with lyso-PS at 54 μM.
Place about 10–15 of 8 to 12-day-old seedlings of each genotype in wells supplemented with or without lyso-PS.
Make sure that the seedlings are drowned in the media.
Transfer the plate in a growth chamber in continuous light conditions at 150 μE.m−2.s−1 and 21°C for an hour.
Use an inverted Zeiss microscope equipped with a spinning disk module and a ProEM+ 1024B camera using a 63× Plan-Apochromat objective.
Turn on the 515 nm laser for mCITRINE excitation (60 mW).
Set fluorescence emission filter to 578/105 nm, using BrightLine® single-band bandpass filter.
Clean the objective before usage applying 70% ethanol using a lens paper.
Mount seedlings on microscope slides.
Mix 75 μL of corresponding liquid ½ MS with or without lyso-PS in the middle of a slide for 60 mm wide cover slips.
Mix approximately 50 μL of corresponding liquid ½ MS with or without lyso-PS in the middle of a slide for 40 mm wide cover slips.
Place about 5 seedlings in the drop on the microscope slide.
Orient the root perpendicular to the main axis of the slide.
Remove the shoot from the seedling with a scalpel.
Place the cover slip gently on the sample to avoid crushing the root.
Dip roots in the corresponding liquid ½ MS before placing plants on the slide.
Add-back liquid ½ MS using a plastic Pasteur pipette if the entire coverslip is not fully covered with liquid ½ MS.
Place a cleaning tissue in the interstice between the slide and the coverslip to absorb excessive water if too much has been added.
Tape the slide and the coverslip together with surgical tape to avoid movement of the cover slip.
Mount the shoot outside of the slide/coverslip sandwich starting from the base of the hypocotyl, if removing the shoot is not required for certain experiments.
Make spacers between the slide and the coverslip using two to three layers of surgical tape around the slide on both sides of the samples.
Ensure that both spacers are of equal thickness on both sides of the samples to maintain parallelism between the slide and the coverslip.
Pour one drop of immersion oil on the objective.
Place the slide on the microscope stage.
Use brightfield to find the root tip.
Adjust x-y-z position to observe the epidermis in the basal meristem.
Acquire images with settings allowing to obtain the best signal/noise ratio and to avoid signal saturation.
Monitor the image dynamic or use the range indicator to ensure optimal settings.
Focus on cells corresponding to the outer layer of the root, larger than the length.
Ensure imaged root has not been damaged by visualizing rectangle cells with a nearly straight plasma membrane.
Transfer seedlings to ½ MS agar plates in a sterile hood.
Use sterile tweezers to transfer 6 seedlings of 8–12 days old, alternating sides on the plate supplemented or not with lyso-PS.
Seal the plates with micropore surgical tape.
Place the plates vertically in a growth chamber.
Maintain continuous light conditions at 150 μE.m−2.s−1 and a temperature of 21°C for 6 days.
Dip tweezers in ethanol 70% and flame dry them by passing quickly into the flame.
Cool down tweezers before transferring plants.
Transfer two seedlings per pot using sterilized tweezers.
Label pots with genotype and media information.
Grow plants in long day (18 h light, 6 h dark) conditions at 21°C for 8 days.
Use a camera and macro objective to take pictures.
Optimize color settings between the rosette and background using automatic settings if necessary.
Place a ruler in one picture for image scale quantification.
Use a camera holder to maintain consistent distance between the objective and plants for all images.
Store each condition and genotype images in separate folders named "To Analyze_Genotype_Condition".
Create an empty folder named "Analyzed_Genotype_Condition" for processed images.
Open images using Fiji software.
Click on Analyze/Set Measurements… to activate “Area box” and click OK.
Set the scale in Fiji by opening an image containing a ruler.
Trace 1 cm on the ruler using the straight-line tool.
Set the scale in Fiji by clicking Analyze/Set Scale….
In the Known distance box, write "1".
In the Unit of length box, write “cm” and activate the “global” mode.
Click OK to confirm settings.
Open the macro file “Macro_Rosette_Size.ijm” in Fiji by dragging it into the tool bar.
Drag the macro file onto the open Fiji window and click “Run”.
Select the folder “To Analyze_Genotype_Condition” for input images.
Click OK after selecting the folder.
Choose the folder “Analyzed_Genotype_Condition” to save processed images.
Process each image to segment the rosette.
If a rosette is separated, click on its parts while holding the shift button and add them in the ROI Manager window by clicking Add [t].
Repeat the step for each subsequent rosette.
Click OK after selecting all parts of a rosette.
Obtain a results window containing the size in cm² for each measured rosette.
